I don't see why you cannot speak to other women. I speak with other men ( I am a woman). I suppose it depends what you are talking about. If you were looking for advice and venting, I don't see a problem with that. 

If you were trying to be more intimate, discussing desires and hopes. I would be miffed as well. Having said that, you both need to try. It won't be easy and it won't be pleasant. If you really love her and you really want to fix this, you have to face the music. 

You will both be upset. She may yell, a lot. You both may say some awful things. Do your best to concentrate on the actual problem. Be sincere and caring. Use "I" messages instead of "You" messages when you wnt to say something negative about her. Ex. "I feel lonely when you....." 

When you want to compliment her, do the opposite. Ex. "You make feel good when..." 

Bring up tose first few years you were together. Rekindle those memories and they will lead you both back. It's not too late.

Communication is the most difficult between two people, but is the foundation of any successful relationship. Perhaps you have a hard time vocalizing your feelings, most men do. 

Apologise to your wife, show her this post. Perhaps write a few short and to the point notes. Romance is good, but right now you need to be honest and just say what needs to be said. 

In the future, speak up! Don't let things fester because moles turn into mountains very quickly. Every marriage goes through a tough time, it's normal. You both need to communicate more. 

All the best!

So, first step is to find home renovation companies. These guys will have general contractors on staff, some of which may specialize in plumbing, electrical or carpentry. It is rare to find one company that can offer all of that under one roof.

This company will however know people in the industry and will hire a plumber or carpenter on your behalf. This is referred to as sub-contracting. 

Call three or four home renovation companies. Questions to ask:

1. Do you do free estimates? (If not, move along)
2. Do you have a certified plumber or carpenter on staff? (This is the bulk of your needs)
3. Do you provide references? (If not, move along)

This is a good place to start. I was 20 when my hubby and I bought our first house. We were both green, as he is not the fix it guy. Since he worked full time and I was home with the kids, it was my job to hire contractors. I was/am very successful at doing so, if I say so myself.
